This scene:
很久以前，古代的人很不知道什么植物能吃，也什么植物不能吃。所以很多人常常吃不安全的植物，吃不安全的植物对你的身体有坏处，很麻烦的情况。但是一个人，神农，要解决这个问题。

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 古代的人很不知道什么植物能吃，也什么植物不能吃：delete很，delete也
- 吃不安全的植物对你的身体有坏处，很麻烦的情况：delete你的，redundant; 是很麻烦的情况
- 但是一个人，神农，要解决这个问题：better to briefly introduce “神农” when this character first appears

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 很不知道：不知道，The adverb 很 cannot modify the mental-state verb 不知道 in this way. [rule: none]
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 也什么植物不能吃：什么植物不能吃，When contrasting two embedded categories, use parallel clauses; 也 cannot directly introduce this noun clause. [teacher rule: ye_vp]
3. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 很麻烦的情况：是一件很麻烦的事，The original is only a noun phrase and cannot finish the sentence after the statement about harm; add a predicate with 是. [rule: none]
4. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 你的身体：他们的身体，The previous sentence names 很多人, so the pronoun should refer back to that group rather than unexpectedly address the reader. [rule: ambiguous_reference]
5. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 一个人，神农：有一个人叫神农，他，A character’s first mention should introduce the person clearly with a full noun phrase and name. [rule: character_introduction_first_mention]

items.reason: 很 cannot modify 不知道 in this construction.
也 cannot directly precede the embedded noun clause 什么植物不能吃.
很麻烦的情况 is only a noun phrase here and needs a predicate such as 是.
你的 unexpectedly addresses the listener instead of referring to the people just mentioned; 他们的 is a valid repair.
神农 needs a clearer first introduction, but the proposed replacement ends with 他 and is incomplete as shown.
